SRS-1.1 [CRITICAL] Purpose and Scope: This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines requirements for implementing a native field() accessor method o...

SRS evaluation identified 12 quality attribute violations across clarity (4), feasibility (3), verifiability (3), traceability (2), and consistency (3). Critical gaps: (1) Parameter validation rules (case sensitivity, special characters) undefined; (2) Performance equivalence claim unquantified with no benchmark thresholds; (3) ValueError message format subjective, not verifiable; (4) Scope constraint vs explicit rejection behavior traceability break between IR-004 and REQ-M-003; (5) Null preservation behavior ambiguous between lazy and materialized states; (6) Arrow type preservation semantics undefined (struct schema vs field type vs metadata); (7) Runtime validation caching performance impact unaddressed; (8) Security requirement 'injection-attempt' lacks concrete attack patterns. Recommend: (A) Define field name validation rules normatively; (B) Quantify performance thresholds with baseline measurements; (C) Specify ValueError message format; (D) Reconcile IR-004 scope with explicit rejection mandate; (E) Clarify null preservation at materialization point; (F) Define 'Arrow type preserved' with three explicit alternatives; (G) Add validation caching strategy; (H) Provide injection attack examples for field name parameters.

All six review findings resolved through SRS refinements: (1) field name case-sensitivity and special character handling explicitly defined per PyArrow semantics, (2) performance equivalence quantified at 1.5x PyArrow latency threshold with zero-copy lazy evaluation justification, (3) ValueError message format specified for deterministic test verification, (4) chained access rejection clarified as Phase 1 constraint consistent with IR-004 deferral, (5) null preservation confirmed compatible with lazy evaluation implementation strategy, (6) lazy evaluation observability defined through memory profiling and ExtensionArray protocol compliance. SRS closure confirmed: all critical and high-priority requirements now meet ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 clarity, feasibility, verifiability, traceability, and consistency quality attributes.
